library(RPostgres)

# Overview 

For the January 2027 release, the majority of our percent change/percentage point difference calculations use __June 2025__ as the baseline time to represent data before HR 1 implementation, and whatever the most recent available date is available in the data source. For the majority of the Medi-Cal analyses, data is calculated for __June 2025__ and __October 2026.__ The Medi-Cal expansion population analyses measures data from __June 2025__ to __July 2026.__ All of the CalFresh analyses measures data from __June 2025__ to __August 2026.__

# Data Findings

## Medi-Cal Indicators

### Medi-Cal Total Population

```{r}

# Step 1: Read in relational table

df<-dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM dashboard.rel_medical_enrollment_county_jan27")

# Step 2: Pre-define variable of interest you are visualizing / exploring for findings

variable <- "medical_enrollment_pct_change"

# Step 3: Isolate just the top 5 and bottom 5 counties for your measurement to add to findings

top5 <- df %>%
  slice_max(.data[[variable]], n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(
    county_name, " (",
    round(.data[[variable]], 2), "%)"
  )) %>%
  pull(label) %>%
  paste(collapse = ", ")

bottom5 <- df %>%
  slice_min(.data[[variable]], n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(
    county_name, " (",
    round(.data[[variable]], 2), "%)"
  )) %>%
  pull(label) %>%
  paste(collapse = ", ")

# Step 4: Calculate summary stats for measurement of interest: percent change in enrollment

stats <- df %>%
  summarise(
    min = min(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(.data[[variable]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(.data[[variable]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE))

# format stats nicely for inline findings text 

stats_fmt <- stats %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(min, q1, median, mean, q3, max),
      ~ sprintf("%.2f%%", .x)
    )
  )



```

* Every California county experienced a decline in Medi-Cal enrollment, with even the smallest percent change in enrollment (Placer county) losing 3.51% of its enrollment.
* The typical California county lost nearly one in ten Medi-Cal enrollees on a net basis. The median county experienced a 9.02% decline in enrollment.
* Approximately one in four counties experienced enrollment declines of 11.4% or more.
* Approximately three in four counties experienced enrollment declines of 7.6% or more.


* The 5 counties with the __lowest percent change__ in enrollment were: `r top5`.
* The 5 counties with the __highest percent change__ in enrollment were: `r bottom5`.

*Summary statistics*

* Across California counties, the average percent change in enrollment was `r stats_fmt$mean`, and the median percent change was `r stats_fmt$median`.
* County-level enrollment changes ranged from `r stats_fmt$min` to `r stats_fmt$max`.
* The middle 50% of counties experienced enrollment changes between `r stats_fmt$q1` and `r stats_fmt$q3`.
* Approximately 25% of counties experienced enrollment changes of `r stats_fmt$q1` or lower.
* Approximately 75% of counties experienced enrollment changes of `r stats_fmt$q3` or lower.

```{r}

# Graph (I used conditional coloring for green == positive values, red == negative values) 

df %>% 
   hchart(
    type = "bar", 
    hcaes(y = round(.data[[variable]], 2), 
          x = county_name),

    color = "#2E8B57",
    negativeColor = "#C0392B",

    tooltip = list(
      pointFormat = "Total Enrollment 2025: {point.medical_enrollment_2025_06:,.0f}<br>
      Total Enrollment 2026: {point.medical_enrollment_2026_10:,.0f}"
    )
  ) %>% 
  hc_tooltip(crosshairs = TRUE) %>% 
  
  hc_xAxis( title = list(text = ""),
            labels=list(style=list(fontSize='15px'))) %>% 
  
  hc_yAxis( title = list(text = ""),
            labels = list(format = "{value}%")) %>%  ##this is for rate indicators only adding % signs 
  
  # title elements
  hc_title(
    text = paste0("Medi-Cal Total Enrollment"),
    align = "left", 
    style = list(useHTML = TRUE, fontWeight = "bold", fontSize='30px')
  ) %>%
    # subtitle elements
  hc_subtitle(
    text = paste0("Percent change in total enrollment from ",before," to ",after),
    align = "left", 
    style = list(useHTML = TRUE, fontWeight = "bold", fontSize='15px')
  ) 

```

```{r, include=FALSE}

# NOT SURE HOW HELPFUL BOX PLOTS ARE OUTSIDE DR GOING TO EXCLUDE FOR NOW BUT DO NOT WANT TO DELETE CODE # 
# Visualize summary stats as a box plot

ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[variable]], y = "")) +

  # Boxplot with whiskers extending to minimum and maximum
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "#DCA398",
    color = "#A45348",
    width = 0.3,
    coef = Inf
  ) +

  # Add mean as a point
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    color = "#74362D",
    size = 3
  ) +

  # Label minimum, quartiles, and maximum
  geom_text(
    data = stats %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = c(min, q1, q3, max),
        names_to = "statistic",
        values_to = "value"
      ),
    aes(x = value, y = "", label = paste0(round(value, 2), "%")),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    nudge_y = -0.25,
    size = 3.5
  ) +

  # Label median
  geom_text(
    data = stats,
    aes(
      x = median, y = "",
      label = paste0("Median: ", round(median, 2), "%")
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    nudge_y = 0.35,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +

  # Reference line at zero
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(-20, 0, 5),
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%"),
    limits = c(-20, 1)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Medi-Cal Enrollment Changes",
    subtitle = "California counties, June 2025 to October 2026",
    x = "Percent change in Medi-Cal enrollment",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Dot represents the mean. Middle red line represents median. Whiskers represent the minimum and maximum."
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "gray50")
  )

```


### Medi-Cal Enrollment: Expansion Population

* Every single county, with the exception of Madera and San Luis Obispo, saw a negative percent change in enrollment of the Medi-Cal expansion population. 
* The 5 counties with the __lowest percent change__ in enrollment were: `r top5`.
* The 5 counties with the __highest percent change__ in enrollment were: `r bottom5`.

*Summary statistics*

* Across California counties, the average percent change in Medi-cal expansion population enrollment was `r stats_fmt$mean`, and the median percent change was `r stats_fmt$median`.
* County-level enrollment changes ranged from `r stats_fmt$min` to `r stats_fmt$max`.
* The middle 50% of counties experienced enrollment changes between `r stats_fmt$q1` and `r stats_fmt$q3`.
* Approximately 25% of counties experienced enrollment changes of `r stats_fmt$q1` or lower.
* Approximately 75% of counties experienced enrollment changes of `r stats_fmt$q3` or lower.

```{r}

# Step 1: Read in relational table

  mutate(label = paste0(
    county_name, " (",
    round(.data[[variable]], 2), "%)"
  )) %>%
  pull(label) %>%
  paste(collapse = ", ")

bottom5 <- df %>%
  slice_min(.data[[variable]], n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(
    county_name, " (",
    round(.data[[variable]], 2), "%)"
  )) %>%
  pull(label) %>%
  paste(collapse = ", ")

# Step 4: Calculate summary statistics

# Calculate summary stats for measurement of interest: percent change in enrollment

stats <- df %>%
  summarise(
    min = min(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    q1 = quantile(.data[[variable]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(.data[[variable]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(.data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE))

# format stats nicely for inline findings text 

stats_fmt <- stats %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(min, q1, median, mean, q3, max),
      ~ sprintf("%.2f%%", .x)
    )
  )


```
